NEW DELHI: Defence minister Rajnath Singh on Wednesday launched a broadside against Congress, accusing it of inciting anarchy through its "regime change" plan.During a speech in Karnataka 's Kalaburagi, Rajnath warned leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi that India's democracy could not be weakened by his party creating ruckus on the streets."Now, when all their tactics have failed, the Congress party and several of their allies say, 'Modi is not going to leave like this; now there must be a regime change here.' By spreading anarchy, spreading unrest, and inciting bloodshed, they want to change the government here," the defence minister said."Regime change has happened in this manner in many of our neighbouring countries; do they want to form a government here by creating similar anarchy?" he asked.Noting that politics should not be a means to capture power but a means to build the nation, he alleged: "The Congress wants regime change through violence and anarchy, not through votes. I want to tell Rahul Gandhi clearly that Indian democracy is not so weak that regime change can happen through anarchy on the streets."Rajnath also said that a change of power in the country could happen "strictly through votes"."Forget the fantasy of regime change that you have imagined by spreading anarchy on the streets," Rajnath said."Power in Hindustan can never be changed by spreading anarchy; if a change of power ever happens, it will happen solely and strictly through votes," he added.During his address, Rajnath also said that Rahul Gandhi was unable to digest the fact that Congress was being rejected everywhere in the country.
Article Summary: Defence minister Rajnath Singh accuses Congress of inciting anarchy through its "regime change" plan. He warns opposition leader Rahul Gandhi that India's democracy cannot be weakened by his party creating ruckus on the streets. He also says that a change of power in the country could happen "strictly through votes"

Article Title: 'Need to halt' vs 'politically motivated session': Jharkhand govt, oppn spar as assembly passes resolution against SIR
Article Text:
The resolution was passed by voice vote

BJP hits back

(With PTI inputs)

NEW DELHI: The Jharkhand assembly on Wednesday passed a resolution demanding an immediate halt to the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The resolution was passed by voice vote following a heated debate.As a special two-day session of the Jharkhand assembly began on Wednesday, finance minister Radha Krishna Kishore moved the resolution opposing the SIR.Leader of opposition and former chief minister Babulal Marandi described the session as "politically motivated" and accused the JMM-led state government of attempting to "mislead" people on the issue.Moving the resolution, Kishore claimed that voters were facing difficulties due to procedural complexities and technical shortcomings in the revision process."Of Jharkhand's 2.21 crore voters, 27% were deemed suspicious and sent notices," PTI quoted him as saying.He called the Election Commission a "puppet" of the BJP-led Centre and asserted that removing Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar was "necessary to protect the Constitution.""There is an urgent need to halt the SIR exercise immediately and to issue a fresh standard operating procedure to ensure transparency in the process," Kishore added.Hitting back at the Jharkhand government, senior BJP leader Babulal Marandi said that the SIR was aimed at purifying electoral rolls, but the state government was creating "confusion" over the exercise."While presenting details, the government concealed the break-up of deleted names. Of the 43 lakh deleted names, 7.63 lakh belonged to deceased voters, 15.53 lakh had shifted, 4.38 lakh were duplicates, and 14.50 lakh were untraceable," he claimed.He maintained that his party opposed any form of administrative negligence but warned that it would not accept attempts to "undermine" the statutory powers of constitutional institutions through "political manoeuvring.""I urge the state government to cooperate with the Election Commission in this (SIR) process, focusing on the inclusion of those who have been left out of the voter's list. I also urge the Election Commission to ensure that the SIR is conducted by taking into account the socio-economic and geographical conditions of Jharkhand," Marandi said.He further argued that halting the electoral roll "purification drive" was not the solution, stressing the need to make the process more transparent, inclusive and accountable.The resolution will now be forwarded to the Centre and other competent authorities, seeking a fresh standard operating procedure (SOP) in consultation with various political parties for transparency.
Article Summary: The resolution was passed by voice vote following a heated debate. Leader of opposition and former chief minister Babulal Marandi described the session as "politically motivated" He accused the JMM-led state government of attempting to "mislead" people on the issue.

Article Title: Passport has discrepancies in place of birth: CJP's Saurav Das rendered ineligible for foreign travel
Article Text:
Saurav Das, chief spokesperson of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), speaks during a press conference in New Delhi, India, November 24, 2026. REUTERS/Bhawika Chhabra

NEW DELHI: A notice served to CJP activist Saurav Das on Monday evening by the Regional Passport Office (RPO), Chennai, asking him to explain alleged discrepancies in his documents relating to place of birth, had rendered his passport ineligible for foreign travel till the response was received and matter resolved.Sources in the govt said the mismatch in birth particulars across different set of documents like aadhaar, passport and birth certificate was flagged in inputs received over the last couple of months, prompting RPO to initiate a fresh verification of documents and information recorded in his passport application file. The passport was issued to him on Aug 21, 2019.While police verification is done either before or after issue of passport (in case of ‘tatkal’ passport), if any adverse or incorrect information comes to light during validity of the passport, a re-verification can be ordered by the RPO by issuing a show-cause notice to the citizen, asking why the passport should not be impounded.A notice was sent to Das by e-mail on Monday evening, asking him to respond within 7 days to the alleged “material suppression of facts” relating to his place of birth. He was asked to clarify the “incorrect” particulars with supporting documents, failing which he could face impounding of his passport under Section 10(b) of the Passports Act, 1967. The notice explicitly advised him not to use his passport till he had filed his response.“As per rules, if a show-cause notice is issued to the passport holder on why his passport should not be impounded in view of furnishing of incorrect particulars, and a reply is awaited, the respondent cannot travel abroad on that passport till the matter is disposed of,” an officer told TOI. “Das was well-aware that the pending RPO notice would be flagged in the immigration systems, preventing his clearance for boarding the flight to London. Yet, he chose to travel to the airport, possibly so he could play the victim after being stopped at immigration,” said the officer.Das, as per reports, however claims he did not see the email, which landed hours before his flight, till he checked his inbox at the immigration counter.A govt officer said Das has time till Nov 30 to respond to the RPO notice. “Let him satisfy the RPO as to which set of birth documents must be relied on. Once the RPO clears him in the re-verification exercise, he can resume international travel on the same passport,” said another officer.Sources explained that disparities were flagged only in the recent past in Das’s details like date of birth and father’s name across documents like aadhaar, passport and school certificate, issued from different places of his residence — Delhi and Puducherry.A PIL has also been filed in the Madras High Court relating to the alleged inconsistencies in his birth and parentage documents and even questioning his citizenship.
Article Summary: Saurav Das, chief spokesperson of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), was served a show-cause notice by the Regional Passport Office (RPO), Chennai. The RPO asked him to explain alleged discrepancies in his documents relating to place of birth. A PIL has also been filed in the Madras High Court relating to the alleged inconsistencies.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Wednesday declined, for now, to grant interim bail to activists Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam in the 2020 northeast Delhi riots "larger conspiracy" case under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA).The two had challenged a Delhi high court order denying them bail.A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana issued notice to the Delhi Police and sought its response on their pleas.During the hearing, senior advocate Kapil Sibal, appearing for Khalid, sought interim bail while the matter was pending. Senior advocate Siddharth Dave, representing Imam, also sought similar relief, citing his prolonged incarceration.However, the bench refused to grant immediate relief, saying, "Not today". It said the Delhi Police would be heard before any decision was taken on the interim bail pleas.The Supreme Court also directed that the matter be placed before the Chief Justice of India on the administrative side for the constitution of a three-judge bench to hear the case.In their petitions, Khalid and Imam have sought bail, arguing that the prosecution has yet to examine protected witnesses and that the one-year embargo imposed by the Supreme Court is nearing its expiry.The case relates to the alleged larger conspiracy behind the February 2020 northeast Delhi riots, which broke out during protests against the Citizenship (Amendment) Act (CAA) and the proposed National Register of Citizens (NRC).Imam was arrested in the case on August 25, 2020, while Khalid was arrested on September 13, 2020.
Article Summary: Supreme Court declines, for now, to grant interim bail to activists Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam. The two had challenged a Delhi high court order denying them bail. The case relates to the alleged larger conspiracy behind the February 2020 northeast Delhi riots.

NEW DELHI: Union minister of state Ramdas Athawale on Wednesday said NCP (SP) chief Sharad Pawar could have been considered for the 2022 presidential election by Prime Minister Narendra Modi had he joined the BJP-led NDA in 2019.Athawale told news agency IANS that he had repeatedly persuaded the veteran politician to join the alliance on the basis of a common minimum programme."I was the one who had suggested that Sharad Pawar should join the NDA in 2019. From 2014 to 2019, Prime Minister Narendra Modi accelerated the country's development, and significant progress was made across several sectors," he said.Athawale said Modi held Pawar in high regard and recalled that the prime minister had considered the NCP (SP) chief his ideal during his tenure as Gujarat chief minister."Prime Minister Narendra Modi believes in development, and our mission is to make India the world's number one economy by 2047. BENGALURU: The Supreme Court on Wednesday cancelled the bail granted to former Congress MLA Vinay Kulkarni in the 2016 murder of BJP worker and Dharwad zilla panchayat member Yogeshgouda Goudar, setting aside the Karnataka High Court’s July 31, 2026 order that suspended his life sentence and stayed his conviction.The apex court’s decision withdraws the relief granted by the high court while Kulkarni’s criminal appeal was pending. The high court had ordered his release on bail after suspending the life sentence imposed by a special court for elected representatives.Kulkarni and 16 others were convicted of murder and criminal conspiracy in the case. The special court sentenced all 17 to life imprisonment after finding them guilty of plotting and executing Goudar’s killing.Goudar, a BJP zilla panchayat member, was hacked to death at a gym in Saptapur, Dharwad, on June 15, 2016. The local police initially investigated the case, which was transferred to the Central Bureau of Investigation in 2019 after allegations of political pressure and claims that Kulkarni, then a district in-charge minister, had orchestrated the killing.The CBI arrested Kulkarni on Nov 5, 2020, naming him the main conspirator.The Supreme Court granted him conditional bail on Aug 11, 2021, with a restriction on entering Dharwad district. It cancelled that bail on June 7, 2025, after allegations of attempts to influence or tamper with witnesses.The apex court granted Kulkarni bail again on Feb 27, 2026, after key witnesses had been examined and directed that the trial be concluded expeditiously. He was convicted along with the other accused on April 15, 2026, and all 17 were sentenced to life imprisonment on April 17.With the Supreme Court now setting aside the high court’s July 31 order, the suspension of Kulkarni’s conviction and life sentence no longer holds. The conviction and sentence will continue to operate, subject to the outcome of his appeal.
Article Summary: Kulkarni and 16 others were convicted of murder and criminal conspiracy in the case. Karnataka High Court’s July 31, 2026 order that suspended his life sentence and stayed his conviction. Goudar, a BJP zilla panchayat member, was hacked to death at a gym in Saptapur, Dharwad.

Article Title: 26 seats vs 120 demand: Why Saharanpur, Gandhi family turfs are testing Congress-SP ties

NEW DELHI: Differences over seat-sharing have surfaced between the Congress and Samajwadi Party ahead of the upcoming Uttar Pradesh assembly elections. The Congress is demanding 120 constituencies, including the Gandhi family's traditional strongholds of Amethi and Raebareli, and is unwilling to settle for fewer seats, news agency ANI reported, citing party sources.Congress conveyed its demand during a meeting with SP leaders in Delhi, where it submitted a list of 120 constituencies it wants to contest, sources told ANI.The list reportedly includes two seats in Saharanpur, where the SP has already announced its candidates, as well as several constituencies in traditional Congress stronghold Raebareli and Amethi, some of which have sitting SP MLAs.On the Congress staking a claim to Amethi and Raebareli, Samajwadi Party leader SP Singh Patel has asserted that the majority of seats in the two neighbouring districts should go to the Akhilesh-led party, arguing that the SP has sitting MLAs there while the Congress does not."Naturally, the party that holds the sitting MLA seats should get them. Furthermore, our own party workers and other leaders have done excellent work, and they deserve to be considered. Therefore, in both Rae Bareli and Amethi, the majority -- or rather, almost all -- of the seats should go to the Samajwadi Party," Patel said.The grand old party's proposed list reportedly includes several constituencies in the Raebareli and Amethi districts, some of which are currently represented by Samajwadi Party MLAs.The demand could emerge as another point of contention between the two parties during their seat-sharing negotiations.Amethi and Raebareli have long been considered the Gandhi family's political turf, with both constituencies playing a significant role in the family's electoral legacy.Amethi's association with the Gandhi family began with Sanjay Gandhi, who won the Lok Sabha seat in 1980. After his death, his brother Rajiv Gandhi won the constituency three consecutive times. The seat later passed to Sonia Gandhi, who won it in 1999 on her political entry, before handing it over to her son Rahul Gandhi.Rahul won Amethi three times, in 2004, 2009 and 2014, before losing to BJP 's actor-turned-politician Smriti Irani in the 2019 Lok Sabha elections.Raebareli, meanwhile, has been associated with the family since the first-ever Lok Sabha elections in 1952, when Feroze Gandhi won the seat. He retained it in 1957 as well. After his death, his wife and former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi represented the constituency, winning in 1967, 1971 and 1980.The seat remained with the family from 2004 onwards, with Sonia Gandhi winning it in four consecutive Lok Sabha elections before making way for Rahul Gandhi, who won Raebareli in the 2024 general elections.While the upcoming contest is for the Uttar Pradesh assembly and not the Lok Sabha, the seats in these two districts continue to hold symbolic significance for the Gandhi family.Meanwhile, SP supremo Akhilesh Yadav has stressed that "winnability" and the larger objective of defeating the BJP should guide the seat-sharing arrangement.In a post on X, Akhilesh called for mutual understanding between the alliance partners and said candidates should be selected based on their electoral prospects. He also emphasised the need for consensus candidates representing the PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak) framework on every seat to take on the BJP.The differences have also triggered sharp reactions within the Congress. Saharanpur MP Imran Masood questioned the SP's reported offer of just 26 seats to the Congress, asking, "Are we beggars?"While the Congress has drawn a line at 120 seats, Akhilesh has indicated that discussions should continue, with the focus on identifying candidates capable of winning rather than dividing constituencies strictly between the two parties.
Article Summary: Congress is demanding 120 constituencies, including the Gandhi family's traditional strongholds of Amethi and Raebareli. Samajwadi Party leader SP Singh Patel has asserted that the majority of seats in the two neighbouring districts should go to the Akhilesh-led party.

Article Title: ‘Lamp could not be lit at designated spot’: Tamil Nadu govt apologises in Supreme Court, contempt plea to be heard in Karthigai Deepam row
Article Text:
‘Lamp could not be lit’: Madurai Collector tells SC, court agrees to hear contempt plea over Deepam row

What happened at Thiruparankundram?

BJP targets INDIA bloc

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Tamil Nadu government on Wednesday apologised before the Supreme Court over the failure to light the traditional Karthigai Deepam lamp at the Deepathoon stone pillar atop Thiruparankundram hill in Madurai district, even as the court said it would hear a contempt plea alleging non-compliance with its directions.A bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi said it would consider the contempt plea and peruse the status report filed by the state government on the developments surrounding the issue.The state government's counsel informed the bench that the traditional lamp had, unfortunately, not been lit at Deepathoon and that a status report detailing the developments had been filed.A senior advocate appearing for the petitioner seeking permission to light the lamp termed the developments "most unfortunate". He alleged deliberate non-compliance with the Supreme Court's directions and urged the bench to initiate suo motu contempt proceedings against the authorities concerned.The petitioner's counsel argued that the flame should have been carried to Deepathoon and the lamp lit there. He also submitted that the state government had repeatedly assured the Madras High Court, until the last moment, that it would comply with the court's directions.When the senior advocate indicated that the petitioners would move a contempt petition, the bench said, "File it, and then we will see."The Supreme Court asked the petitioner and other parties to file appropriate applications, assuring them that the matter would be heard.The controversy centres on the traditional practice of lighting the Karthigai Deepam lamp at Deepathoon, a stone pillar atop Thiruparankundram hill. The Supreme Court had permitted the ceremonial lighting at the location on November 24 as a one-time measure.However, the lamp was not lit at Deepathoon on Tuesday evening. Instead, the Maha Deepam was lit at the Ucchi Pillayar temple.The Madurai district collector's status report informed the Supreme Court that the ceremonial lamp could not be lit at the designated pillar despite its directions. The state government has cited law-and-order restrictions and customary practices in opposing the lighting at the disputed location. It also told the court that the temple's Board of Trustees had not authorised the team tasked with carrying out the exercise.The dispute has triggered protests by Hindu organisations across Tamil Nadu, with demonstrators accusing the state government of disregarding the Supreme Court's directions. Several protesters were detained after road blockades in parts of the state.BJP leader Sudhanshu Trivedi on Wednesday accused the Tamil Nadu government and the INDIA bloc of failing to comply with the Supreme Court's order, calling the episode the "biggest constitutional contempt"."Today, I want to draw your attention to what we consider the biggest constitutional contempt committed by the INDI alliance Tamil Nadu government. On the occasion of Kartik Purnima yesterday, the Tamil Nadu government did not comply with the Supreme Court's order allowing the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam for just one day, subject to certain conditions. They have neither followed nor implemented the Supreme Court's judgment," he said at a press conference.Trivedi also questioned Congress leader Rahul Gandhi over his repeated references to the Constitution, alleging that the party and its allies were not upholding the Supreme Court's directions."Eradication of Sanatan Dharma is motivated by the evil intention of the INDIA alliance," he said.He further compared the controversy to the Shah Bano case, saying, "It will be another Shah Bano event of Congress alliance."Earlier on Wednesday, organisations including the Hindu Front and Hindu Munnani staged protests in several parts of Tamil Nadu over the non-lighting of the lamp at Deepathoon. In Ramanathapuram, police detained protesters who blocked a road, while members of Hindu Munnani staged a road blockade in Pollachi.
Article Summary: The controversy centres on the traditional practice of lighting the Karthigai Deepam lamp at Deepathoon, a stone pillar atop Thiruparankundram hill. The Supreme Court had permitted the ceremonial lighting at the location on November 24 as a one-time measure. The dispute has triggered protests by Hindu organisations across Tamil Nadu.

Article Title: Congress to hold nationwide ‘Samvidhan Raksha’ marches on Thursday; Kharge to lead from Lucknow

NEW DELHI: Congress will organise ‘Samvidhan Raksha’ Marches across all states on Thursday to mark Constitution Day , with party President Mallikarjun Kharge to participate from Lucknow.The party is stepping up its campaign ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections.According to a statement quoted by ANI news agency, All India Congress Committee (AICC) general secretary KC Venugopal said every Pradesh Congress Committee (PCC) would organise a march in its respective state.The marches will begin at statues of BR Ambedkar or Mahatma Gandhi. Congress workers and participants will pay tribute, read the Preamble aloud and take an oath to protect the Constitution, recalling its principles of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity.Alongside the marches, party workers will visit every polling booth under the Vote Rakshak campaign to verify the names of voters deleted from electoral rolls and help them reclaim their right to vote.Venugopal appealed to students, youth, farmers, workers, women, Dalit, Adivasi, OBC and minority communities, as well as civil society members and other citizens who value the Constitution, to participate in the marches."The Constitution gave every Indian the vote. The Indian National Congress is duty-bound and committed to defend it," he said, as per ANI.The Congress also raised concerns over alleged irregularities in electoral rolls. Venugopal referred toRahul Gandhi 's allegations of "Vote Chori", citing fake and duplicate entries in Mahadevapura, attempts to delete thousands of genuine voters in Aland, and alleged irregularities in Haryana and other states.He alleged that the Election Commission of India had dismissed the findings instead of ordering an impartial inquiry, sought affidavits from the leader of opposition and failed to share information requested by investigating agencies.Venugopal also criticised the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, which began months before the Bihar Assembly elections and has since been expanded to several states and Union Territories. He said the exercise, despite its stated aim of ensuring clean electoral rolls, had made citizens prove their eligibility.
Article Summary: Congress will organise ‘Samvidhan Raksha’ Marches across all states on Thursday. Party President Mallikarjun Kharge to participate from Lucknow. Marches will begin at statues of BR Ambedkar or Mahatma Gandhi.

Article Title: ‘Not a single bogus vote to be added’: Akhilesh tells SP workers to monitor election commission activities
Article Text:
SP chief Akhilesh Yadav ( Photo: PTI).

NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav on Wednesday urged the party's 'PDA sentinels' across Uttar Pradesh to monitor the Election Commission 's electoral roll activities ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections.In a post on X, Yadav asked party workers across the state to remain vigilant about the poll body's activities, with two principles for monitoring changes to voter lists: "Not a single bogus vote to be added, not a single genuine vote to be removed!"The SP chief also raised concerns over the credibility of Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs), referring to public scepticism about the voting system."How can we trust them, when ‘Haathi ke daant khaane ke aur, dikhaane keaur’ (All show, no substance)," Yadav said.In his post, the party chief also mentioned the controversy surrounding the Chandigarh mayoral election, referring to what he called the BJP 's 'Chandigarh trick'. He said people were aware of the episode and understood such political tactics.The Chandigarh mayoral election controversy centres on allegations of deliberate ballot tampering by presiding officer Anil Masih during the January 30, 2024, mayoral polls. The Supreme Court subsequently found that Masih had deliberately marked eight ballot papers cast in favour of Aam Aadmi Party (AAP)-Congress candidate Kuldeep Kumar, leading to their wrongful rejection. Later, the apex court quashed the initially declared result and declared Kumar the validly elected mayor of Chandigarh.On Tuesday, Yadav urged the Congress to identify more potential constituencies beyond the 26 seats on its priority list as the two parties negotiate a seat-sharing arrangement for Assembly elections, ANI reported.He said the discussions should be conducted in the name of the INDIA alliance rather than being limited to candidates from either the Samajwadi Party or the Congress. Yadav described the two parties' cooperation as a "historic opportunity" to defeat what he called the "communal BJP and its narrow-minded allies".He called for serious discussions that take public expectations and political realities into account, saying the alliance should aim to win in as many constituencies as possible."Among the seats you and we contest, the number we win should exceed the number we lose. Only victory will make the division of seats respectable, because only the seats we win will bring us respect," he said.Yadav also asked the Congress to share the names of all other constituencies it considered winnable, apart from the 26 already discussed. He said both parties could then assess the prospects of potential candidates in each seat.
Article Summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav urges party's 'PDA sentinels' across Uttar Pradesh to monitor the Election Commission's electoral roll activities. Yadav also raised concerns over the credibility of Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs)

Article Title: 'Udta Punjab' to 'Ubharta Punjab': BJP's Tarun Chugh pitches drug-free, gangs-free state

Article Title: Congress seeks 130 seats in UP, SP offers '26 winnable' ones
Article Text:
SP-Cong alliance on table





LUCKNOW: Samajwadi Party offered Congress 26 constituencies as seat-sharing negotiations for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections stretched to 3.5 hours in New Delhi on Tuesday, with both sides claiming progress but no breakthrough after media reports said Congress tabled a list of 130 of its choice.SP chief Akhilesh Yadav stressed that winnability would guide seat-sharing. "Beginning has been made with the 'first 26 winnable seats'. Working together with mutual understanding, the talks will move further forward," he posted in Hindi on X.Akhilesh's emphasis on winnability had earlier found support from Congress MP Rahul Gandhi during a meeting with UP party netas on alliance strategy and preparations for the 2027 polls.After the meeting on Day 2, which was considerably longer than Monday's 15-minute opening round, the SP chief urged alliance partners to accommodate each other. "We should adjust and accommodate so that we can defeat our rivals. That's the biggest responsibility of political parties," he said.SP general secretary Ram Gopal Yadav, who headed his party's negotiating team, had made the 26-seat announcement before Tuesday's meeting.These seats include two held by Congress MLAs and four where the party finished second. "There are 20 seats where SP got 70,000 votes while Congress managed 2,000 votes," he said, adding that seat-sharing could not be done at the cost of losing elections.Both parties said they hoped to reach an understanding when negotiations resumed, possibly later this week. Denying differences and acrimony during talks, Congress functionary Pramod Tiwari said they were held "in a cordial atmosphere" and progressing at a positive note. "The common agenda of SP and Congress is to defeat BJP in UP," he said.Saharanpur MP and Congress negotiator Imran Masood insisted his party was not begging. "There is a difference between 'demanding' seats and 'cooperating' - you don't have to demand anything in an alliance. Within an alliance, it's a matter of cooperation. We'll sit down and talk it out," he said.The Saharanpur MP also sounded confident of a consensus within days. "We are discussing everything, not just the candidate for the seat. We plan a strong alliance on all 403 seats," Masood said.Congress functionaries claimed more than 100 seats had figured at Tuesday's meeting. "Had the discussion been around only 26 seats, it would not have lasted more than three-and-a-half hours," one functionary said. "There is no guarantee of victory on any seat. In a democracy, veterans may lose, underdogs may win. The only thing in hand is to put the best foot forward."UPCC president Aradhana Misra said both the sides had agreed to discuss every seat and would soon decide the date for the next round.
Article Summary: Samajwadi Party offers Congress 26 constituencies as seat-sharing negotiations for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections stretch to 3.5 hours. Both sides claim progress but no breakthrough after media reports said Congress tabled a list of 130 of its choice.

Article Title: ‘Siddaramaiah, Mahadevappa to attend Constitution Day event:n

Rejecting reports of a political rift over the event and the alleged omission of Mahadevappa’s photos from publicity banners, Yathindra said the allegations are baseless.

Article Title: Ramgarh police rescue abducted Ranchi land broker, arrest five
Article Text:
Patratu ASP cum SDPO Raghvendra Sharma with the five arrested accused on Wednesday

Ramgarh:





A Ranchi-based land broker, who was allegedly abducted from Bhurkunda market in Ramgarh district on Monday, was rescued near a forest in Pithoria of Ranchi. Five persons have been arrested in the case, police said on Wednesday.Patratu ASP-cum-SDPO Raghvendra Sharma said, "Kamlesh Thakur (42) alias Dinesh Sharma, a native of Harli village in Barkagaon block of Hazaribag and resident of Pandra, Ranchi, was abducted from Bhurkunda market between 4pm and 5pm on Nov 23. Acting on a complaint lodged by his wife, Rinku Devi, Bhurkunda police registered a case. The accused allegedly abandoned Thakur near a forest in Pithoria of Ranchi, from where he was rescued the next day. ”“The accused, who were travelling in a white car from Ranchito Hazaribag, were arrested from near Law College at Hosir on Ranchi Ring Road on the night of Nov 24. They were identified as Raushan Kumar Singh (30), Dharmendra Kumar Saw (31), Rajmani Gupta alias Bunty (37), Ghanshyam Singh (43), all residents of Ranchi, and Piyush Kumar (21) of Ramgarh. The car and four mobile phones were seized,” the SDPO added.Preliminary investigation revealed that a dispute over money transactions and personal enmityled to the abduction. The accused allegedly followed Thakur from Ranchi before abducting him from Bhurkunda and taking him through Urimari, Barkagaon, Keredari and Tandwa, to Gumla, where he was assaulted. Raushan has a criminal case registered against him by ATS in 2024 under provisions of the BNS and UAPA, police said.
Article Summary: Kamlesh Thakur (42) alias Dinesh Sharma, a native of Harli village in Barkagaon block of Hazaribag and resident of Pandra, Ranchi, was abducted from Bhurkunda market between 4pm and 5pm on Nov 23. Five persons have been arrested in the case, police said on Wednesday.

Article Title: ​Rajya Sabha MP Wadkute passes away
Article Text:
Ramrao Wadkute

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





Rajya Sabha member and BJP leader Ramrao Wadkute died at AIIMS in New Delhi late on Saturday after suffering a severe heart attack. He was 72.Wadkute was admitted to AIIMS on Nov 20 after complaining of cough and chest discomfort. He suffered a heart attack and died while undergoing treatment, party leaders said.A resident of Kalamnuri in Hingoli district, Wadkute was a prominent leader of the Dhangar community in Marathwada and was known as a simple, grassroots politician.Condoling his death, chief minister Devendra Fadnavis said Wadkute’s demise was the loss of a simple and dedicated political leader who was deeply committed to grassroots welfare.“He shouldered many organizational responsibilities for the BJP in Hingoli district. He did a great deal of work for the Dhangar community. He left his mark on the cooperative sector as well. His concern for grassroots communities was always evident,” the CM said.Wadkute began his political career with Nationalist Congress Party and served as a member of Maharashtra Legislative Council from June 2014 to Oct 2019. He was also president of Punyashlok Ahilyadevi Maharashtra Sheep and Goat Development Corporation Limited.He left the NCP in Oct 2019 and joined the BJP. In 2021, he was appointed BJP’s Hingoli district president. He also served as the party’s election chief and in-charge for the Hingoli Lok Sabha constituency. The BJP nominated him for the Rajya Sabha from Maharashtra in March this year.BJP Hingoli district president Gajanan Ghuge said last rites on Wadkute were scheduled on Tuesday morning. “His body will be flown to Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar on Monday, and will be taken to Parbhani first and later at Hingoli. The last rites will be performed when his daughter arrives from the US,” he said.Wadkute is survived by his wife, two sons and a daughter.
Article Summary: Wadkute was admitted to AIIMS on Nov 20 after complaining of cough and chest discomfort. He suffered a heart attack and died while undergoing treatment, party leaders said. He was a prominent leader of the Dhangar community in Marathwada.

Article Title: Raut claims Rs 150cr being offered to MPs to back delimitation bill, Mahajan says allegations childish

File photo

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut claimed on Saturday that MPs were being offered “Rs 150 crore to back the proposed delimitation bill”, even as BJP minister Girish Mahajan dismissed it as a “childish allegation”.Raut also said that BJP would not return to power in 2029 if the current political atmosphere and public pressure continued. He added that Congress party’s performance in Rajasthan’s panchayat elections reflected the country’s changing mood.Interacting with the media during his visit to Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar on Saturday, Raut alleged that BJP was attempting to secure support for the proposed delimitation bill and questioned why a Parliament session was not being convened.“Remember this figure if Maharashtra ’s MPs support the bill,” Raut said, alleging that some prominent politicians in the state had been entrusted with arranging the money and securing support. He also questioned Union home minister Amit Shah ’s frequent visits to Mumbai over the past two months, alleging that political negotiations were being conducted from the city.BJP minister Girish Mahajan, speaking in Jalgaon, said that Raut makes “childish allegations.No one takes him seriously anymore.”Raut said Congress’s good performance in Rajasthan’s panchayat samiti and zilla parishad elections was the outcome of public pressure preventing electoral malpractice and keeping the election machinery under check. “If this public pressure continues until 2029, the BJP will not return to power. It is not 100% but 500% certain,” he said.

Article Title: Row over how much senior counsels were paid to appear for hearing over petition challenging co-op ordinance passed by Maha govt
Article Text:
Kolhapur:





Congress MLC Satej Patil has accused Mahayuti govt of spending Rs 80 lakh on senior advocate Mukul Rohatgi to defend an ordinance allowing four nominated members voting rights in major cooperatives. BJP hit back, claiming Patil too spent Rs 1.8 crore to engage senior advocate Abhishek Manu Singhvi for the same hearing, including Rs 1 crore on a chartered flight.Patil shared on social media a state govt resolution dated Nov 23 approving Rs 80 lakh as Rohatgi’s fee for appearing before Bombay high court’s vacation bench on Nov 9.“Mahayuti govt brought the ordinance to overturn the mandate given to our panel in the Gokul dairy election. It then spent Rs 80 lakh to ensure the ordinance passed the legal test,” Patil said. “If the ordinance was legally sound, why was there a need to engage a senior constitutional lawyer? Govt is normally represented by experienced lawyers under the advocate general. Instead, it chose to bring in senior counsel. ”Rohatgi appeared online for the state, while Singhvi represented 13 directors of the Patil-led panel. The high court declined to stay the ordinance, following which Mahayuti won the Gokul dairy chairman’s election with the support of four nominated directors.BJP spokesperson Navnath Ban defended the payment to Rohatgi and levelled a countercharge against Patil. “Govt-panel counsel are paid according to the rules, and Rohatgi was paid Rs 80 lakh accordingly. I want to ask Satej Patil where the Rs 1.8 crore he allegedly spent on one hearing came from,” Ban said.Ban claimed Patil spent Rs 1 crore on a chartered flight to fly Singhvi between Delhi and Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar for the Nov 9 hearing and another Rs 80 lakh on his legal fee.Minister Hasan Mushrif said senior counsel are engaged when required to strongly present govt’s case and suggested the advocate general’s absence may have necessitated Rohatgi’s engagement.“Govt has paid the fee for the services it sought. So far, we have spent from our own pockets to fight the case,” Mushrif said.
Article Summary: Congress MLC Satej Patil accused Mahayuti govt of spending Rs 80 lakh on senior advocate Mukul Rohatgi to defend an ordinance allowing four nominated members voting rights in major cooperatives. BJP hit back, claiming Patil too spent Rs 1.8 crore to engage senior advocate Abhishek Manu Singhvi for the same hearing.

Article Title: 25,000 autorickshaws stay off roads in Kolhapur
Article Text:
Around 25,000 autorickshaws stayed off Kolhapur’s roads on Monday during a statewide strike against app-based bike-taxi services such as Rapido and Uber, leaving students, commuters and tourists scrambling for transport.

Kolhapur

:





Around 25,000 autorickshaws stayed off Kolhapur’s roads on Monday during a statewide strike against app-based bike-taxi services such as Rapido and Uber , leaving students, commuters and tourists scrambling for transport.Drivers also protested outside the district collector’s office and submitted a memorandum to collector Vijay Rathod. Their key demands are a permanent ban on bike taxis, exemption for autorickshaws from automated vehicle testing and mandatory permits for e-rickshaws.The unions alleged that app-based bike taxis were carrying passengers without mandatory commercial permits, driver badges and yellow number plates. They claimed this was hurting the livelihoods of licensed auto and taxi drivers and raised passenger safety concerns.They also opposed mandatory fitness tests at privately operated automated testing stations. The unions alleged that even well-maintained autos were being declared unfit, imposing additional costs on drivers.They demanded permits for e-rickshaws, alleging many were operating without permits or driving licences and creating unfair competition for licensed operators.Union leader Rajendra Jadhav urged govt to address the drivers’ concerns. He also appealed to deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde to intervene.“Growing regulatory hurdles and unauthorised services are making it increasingly difficult for drivers to support their families and educate their children,” Jadhav said.Congress MLC Satej Patil visited the protest and backed the drivers. “Nearly 15 lakh autorickshaw drivers across Maharashtra contribute significantly to govt revenue. Yet, govt is destroying the livelihoods of these hardworking people. Only five to eight drivers in Kolhapur district have benefited from the welfare boards announced by the govt,” Patil said.The unions threatened to intensify the agitation in phases across Maharashtra if state and central govts failed to address their demands.
Article Summary: Around 25,000 autorickshaws stayed off Kolhapur’s roads on Monday during a statewide strike against app-based bike-taxi services such as Rapido and Uber. Their key demands are a permanent ban on bike taxis, exemption for autorickhaws from automated vehicle testing and mandatory permits for e-rickshaws.

NAVI MUMBAI: A 25-year-old woman on Monday lodged a rape complaint at CBD-Belapur police station against habitual offender Shailendra Dwivedi (50), who allegedly posed as a journalist.Dwivedi was arrested by Ulwe police on November 12 in a cheating and criminal breach of trust case for allegedly duping Thane trader Vijay Jha and four others of Rs 19 lakh in a flat sale deal. He is currently lodged in Taloja jail.Senior inspector Arun Pawar of CBD-Belapur police station said the woman alleged that on May 30 last year, she had attended a birthday party at Arush Hotel in Sector 15, CBD-Belapur, and was also there to collect Rs 10,000 from Jha. He also threatened to circulate an intimate video, which he had allegedly recorded on his mobile phone.Pawar said, "The woman claimed that she did not approach the police earlier because of Dwivedi's threats.After learning that he had been arrested in another case and lodged in jail, she came forward and registered an FIR against him."Police have invoked relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) relating to rape, administering stupefying or intoxicating substances, aggravated criminal intimidation and intentional insult with intent to provoke a breach of public peace.(The victim's identity has not been revealed to protect her privacy as per Supreme Court directives on cases related to sexual assault)
Article Summary: A 25-year-old woman on Monday lodged a rape complaint at CBD-Belapur police station against habitual offender Shailendra Dwivedi (50), who allegedly posed as a journalist. Article Title: FDA, cops bust illegal scented tobacco manufacturing unit in Loni Kalbhor
Article Text:
An AI-generated illustration shows police and FDA officials raiding an illegal scented tobacco manufacturing unit

Pune:





In a joint operation, the crime branch of the city police and Food and Drug Administration (FDA) busted an illegal scented tobacco manufacturing unit at Loni Kalbhor.A case was registered with the Loni Kalbhor police. Police seized a tobacco processing machine, tobacco and packaging material collectively worth Rs 12 lakh and arrested one person.An officer from the Pune crime branch said an FDA official had received a tip-off about an illegal scented tobacco manufacturing unit operating in Loni Kalbhor.“In the early hours of Sunday, we raided the unit along with FDA officials and found scented tobacco being manufactured and packed there,” the officer said.He said the police had arrested a 26-year-old man who owned the machine and other materials. KALLAKURICHI: Tirupur superintendent of police Shristi Singh arrived in Kallakurichi to commence investigation into the sexual harassment complaint filed by a woman district collector against Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) MLA C Arul Vignesh.After receiving the case files from local police at the Kallakurichi all-women police station (AWPS), Shristi Singh took charge. Article Title: Tamil Nadu govt forms internal complaints committee to probe woman officer’s complaint against Kallakurichi TVK MLA Arul Vignesh
Article Text:
Kallakurichi TVK MLA C Arul Vignesh





CHENNAI: The Tamil Nadu govt on Wednesday constituted an internal complaints committee (ICC) to inquire into a woman officer’s complaint alleging sexual harassment against Kallakurichi MLA C Arul Vignesh.The committee will be headed by environment, climate change and forest additional chief secretary Kakarla Usha, welfare of differently abled persons secretary S Madumathi, law secretary P Sumathi and Sunitha Joe are the other members.A govt order cited “representation from a lady officer on Nov 23, 2026,” for setting up the committee.The order said the committee had been constituted to inquire into the complaint against the MLA, who represents the Kallakurichi assembly constituency. “The committee shall make efforts to complete the inquiry within 60 days,” the order said.The govt order was issued by chief secretary M Sai Kumar.The panel has also been directed to take further action, as necessary, under the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 on the said complaint. The standard operating procedure for conducting an inquiry under the Act is set out in a govt order issued by the social welfare and women empowerment department on June 18, 2025, the order said.
Article Summary: The committee will be headed by environment, climate change and forest additional chief secretary Kakarla Usha. The panel has also been directed to take further action, as necessary, under the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act.

Article Title: Land surveyor, middleman booked for accepting bribe near Coimbatore
Article Text: COIMBATORE: The Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) has registered a case against a land surveyor and a middleman in Sulur for accepting a bribe of Rs 25,000 to survey a parcel of land and facilitate the issuance of a separate patta.The accused have been identified as Balamurugan, 35, a govt-licensed land surveyor attached to the Sulur taluk office, and Praveenkumar, 32, who runs an e-service centre in the area.According to DVAC officials, Arun Kumar, a milk trader from Pollachi, owns a piece of land at Kalangal near Sulur. He approached Balamurugan in late August to survey the property and provide the necessary documents for obtaining a separate patta. Balamurugan demanded Rs 20,000 to survey the property and recommend to the tahsildar the issuance of a separate patta. Unwilling to pay the bribe, Arun Kumar lodged a complaint with the chief minister’s special cell.After learning about the complaint, Balamurugan increased the demand by Rs 5,000 and insisted that Arun Kumar pay Rs 25,000. He allegedly instructed him to transfer the money through GPay to Praveenkumar, the middleman.Arun Kumar transferred the amount, following which the property was surveyed, and the documents were handed over to him.Arun Kumar subsequently informed the Coimbatore DVAC officials about the bribery. After obtaining govt permission, the DVAC registered a case under the Prevention of Corruption Act against both men on Tuesday. Further investigation is under way.
Article Summary: The Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) has registered a case against a land surveyor and a middleman in Sulur. The accused have been identified as Balamurugan, 35, and Praveenkumar, 32, who runs an e-service centre in the area.

Article Title: Man held for damaging two Karunanidhi statues, glass panels of DMK library and office in Erode
Article Text:
The Erode district police launched an intensive investigation and examined CCTV footage. The footage revealed that the same man had visited the various locations and caused the damage.





ERODE: The Erode district police on Tuesday arrested a man on charges of damaging two statues of late Tamil Nadu chief minister M Karunanidhi , a library and a DMK party office.The incidents came to light after the spectacles on the Karunanidhi statue at Panneerselvam Park in Erode were found broken. The Karunanidhi statue at Alangattu Valasu in Modakkurichi was also damaged.“The glass panels of a library situated beneath Karunanidhi’s statue in the Municipal Colony area were damaged. In another incident, the front glass facade of the DMK district headquarters at Manalmedu was found shattered,” said a party functionary.The Erode district police launched an intensive investigation and examined CCTV footage. The footage revealed that the same man had visited the various locations and caused the damage.“Based on the investigation, police identified the suspect as Hari Vignesh, 26, of Thottipalayam Pudur near Modakkurichi,” said superintendent of police D V Kiran Shruthi. The man, who was drunk on Monday night, also damaged the doors and window panes of his own house as well as the windows of some vehicles.Police said legal action would be initiated. Preliminary inquiries indicated that the man might be suffering from mental health-related issues.
Article Summary: The incidents came to light after the spectacles on the Karunanidhi statue at Panneerselvam Park in Erode were found broken. The glass panels of a library situated beneath the statue were also damaged. The front glass facade of the DMK district headquarters at Manalmedu was found shattered.

Article Title: Man arrested for assaulting police constable in Coimbatore
Article Text: COIMBATORE: A 37-year-old man was arrested on charges of assaulting and abusing a police constable while the latter was on duty at Kurichi in the city on Sunday.The arrested man has been identified as G Boopathi of Gandhi Road near Kurichi.According to police, S Sanjeev Gandhi, a Grade II police constable attached to the Sundarapuram police station, was on patrol duty with a police inspector near the Indian National Congress party office on Sunday. Boopathi, a committee member of the Aravan temple, picked an argument with the constable over a temple festival. During the argument, he grabbed the constable’s uniform, pushed and abused him, obstructed him from discharging his official duties and threatened to murder anyone who tried to stop him. Onlookers intervened and separated him from the cop.Sanjeevanandhi lodged a complaint with the Sundarapuram police on Sunday. Police registered a case under sections 296(b), 132 and 351(2) of BNS.Boopathi was remanded in judicial custody.
Article Summary: A 37-year-old man was arrested on charges of assaulting and abusing a police constable while the latter was on duty at Kurichi in the city on Sunday. The arrested man has been identified as G Boopathi of Gandhi Road near Kurichi. He was remanded in judicial custody.

Article Title: TNEB employee held with ganja in Mettur
Article Text:
Salem





: A suspended electricity board employee was arrested on Saturday for smuggling ganja on his two-wheeler in Mettur.Police identified the arrested person as M Joseph, 47, of Matha Kovil area in Mettur. According to an investigation officer, Joseph was nabbed while they were conducting a routine vehicle check along the right bank of Mettur dam on Kolathur Road.“He was riding a two-wheeler in a suspicious manner. Upon inspecting the vehicle, we found 900 grams of ganja concealed inside the seat cover. We seized the contraband and took Joseph to the police station for interrogation.”Investigations revealed that Joseph was already facing a ganja smuggling case, which had led to his suspension from the electricity board.Police registered a case, arrested him and produced him before the Mettur court, which remanded him in judicial custody. Article Title: Traffic diversions announced in Krishnagiri in view of festivals
Article Text:
traffic diversions

Krishnagiri

:





District police have announced traffic diversions for heavy vehicles and non-pilgrim traffic from 2pm on November 22 to 6am on November 26, in view of Tiruvannamalai Maharatham and Karthigai Deepam festivals.In a media statement, SP GS Anitha stated that heavy vehicles travelling from Bengaluru to Tiruvannamalai , Villupuram, Cuddalore and Puducherry must take the Krishnagiri-Vaniyambadi-Vellore-Cheyyar-Vandavasi-Tindivanam route instead of proceeding through Uthangarai, Chengam and Tiruvannamalai.Vehicles from Bengaluru bound for Vriddhachalam, Chidambaram and Nagapattinam through Krishnagiri will be diverted via Dharmapuri, Thoppur, Salem, Vazhapadi, and Attur.Vehicles from Bargur towards Tiruvannamalai and those arriving through Kuppam will be diverted via Vaniyambadi, Vellore, Cheyyar, Vandavasi, and Tindivanam. Heavy vehicles arriving from Dharmapuri through Manjamedu will be diverted at Puliyur Junction towards Tiruvannamalai Road instead of Pochampally Road.Heavy vehicles travelling from Krishnagiri towards Tiruvannamalai will be diverted to Bargur Road at Jagadevi.All vehicles heading from Krishnagiri to Tiruvannamalai will also be diverted at Kannandahalli near Mathur police station towards Tirupattur.Heavy vehicles using Krishnagiri bypass roads will be diverted at Uthangarai MGR Nagar through Karapattu, Kathavani and Arunapathi toll road towards Tirupattur. Those arriving from Salem via Harur and Uthangarai for Tiruvannamalai will also be redirected through Tirupattur.Heavy vehicles travelling from Tirupattur towards Tiruvannamalai via Singarapettai and Chengam will be rerouted towards Tirupattur. Vehicles from Dharmapuri district proceeding via Irumathur, Puliyur, and Olapatti will use alternative routes notified by police.The SP explained the arrangements at a consultation meeting with truck drivers’ welfare association office-bearers at the district police office and sought their cooperation.
Article Summary: Heavy vehicles travelling from Bengaluru to Tiruvannamalai must take the Krishnagiri-Vaniyambadi-Vellore-Cheyyar-Vandavasi-Tindivanam route. Vehicles from Dharmapuri district proceeding via Irumathur, Puliyur, and Olapatti will use alternative routes.

COIMBATORE: Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) has permanently removed Prakash , the party’s Vadavalli town secretary, from his post and all party responsibilities following a video of him creating a ruckus inside a two-wheeler showroom circulated on social media.The announcement stated that the action was taken following a video circulated in the media and complaints from party functionaries.The party said Prakash had allegedly acted in a manner contrary to its policies, objectives and principles, bringing disrepute to the organisation.The order, signed by V Raghukumar, Coimbatore North district secretary of TVK, said Prakash had been removed permanently from all party posts and even the primary membership to maintain discipline within the organisation.Earlier, a video of him making a ruckus inside a two-wheeler showroom near Vadavalli in the city was circulated on social media.In the video, a woman was alleging that Prakash received a bribe to give her a party posting. Article Title: 864 bottles of liquor seized from house near Erode; man arrested
Article Text: ERODE: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district in the early hours of Thursday and arrested a man.Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid at the house of K Govindaraj, 28, of Ammapalayam. They found 864 bottles of IMFL stocked in the house for illegal sale.Police registered a case and arrested Govindaraj. He was remanded in judicial custody.They launched a search for Sekar alias Ammasai, 34, and Sridhar, 38, who have links with the illegal liquor operation.
Article Summary: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district. Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid.

SALEM: A govt school teacher was arrested in Salem district on Sunday night under sections of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act on charges of inappropriate behaviour towards girl students.The arrested teacher, M Sankar, 49, of Vinayagapuram, is serving as a social science teacher in a govt school in the district.According to the complaint, the teacher allegedly made inappropriate remarks to Class X girl students on Nov 5. “He is accused of making a heart-shaped hand gesture towards one student and calling another student ‘Cleopatra’ while commenting on the beauty of her eyes,” said an officer at the all women police station in Attur.The students brought the matter to the notice of the headmaster on Nov 13. The headmaster informed chief educational officer A Ellappan and contacted Childline 1098 seeking intervention.Following the complaint, a member of the child welfare committee visited the school on Nov 14 and conducted an inquiry into the allegations raised by the students.Based on the findings, the headmaster lodged a complaint with the Attur all women police on Sunday. Article Title: Yadav: 38% of electorate affected during voter roll revision
Article Text:
Pradeep Yadav waves the list of voters allegedly wrongly deleted from Santhal Pargana towards opposition benches on Wednesday

Ranchi:





Congress Legislature Party leader Pradeep Yadav on Wednesday demanded an immediate halt to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Jharkhand, alleging it had affected nearly 38% of voters and risked disenfranchising eligible electors.Backing state govt’s resolution against SIR in the assembly, the Poraiyahat MLA sought a transparent standard operating procedure and a fresh revision based on the 2024 rolls. “I urged the assembly to adopt a resolution seeking suspension of SIR, a fresh exercise based on the 2024 rolls and removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar of failing to ensure a transparent revision,” he said.Citing figures during the debate in the House, Yadav said Jharkhand had around 2.64 crore voters before SIR, of whom nearly 43.62 lakh, or 16.48%, were excluded from the draft roll. Of around 2.21 crore voters retained, 59.59 lakh, or 26.94%, subsequently received notices, including around 45.55 lakh cases classified under “logical discrepancy” and 14.04 lakh under “no-mapping”.Combining exclusions and notices, Yadav claimed over 38% of the electorate had been affected. “Why people who had voted for years are being required to repeatedly establish their eligibility?” he asked.Yadav questioned chief electoral officer K Ravi Kumar and the handling of Forms 6, 7 and 8, alleging procedures could facilitate wrongful deletion or inclusion of voters. Citing alleged irregularities in Maharashtra and SIR’s impact in West Bengal, he questioned the Election Commission ’s independence.Targeting BJP and leader of opposition Babulal Marandi, he said, “They are only speaking the language of EC and have stopped fighting for the people’s issues.”Opposing the resolution, Marandi said, “JMM-led coalition govt is only misleading the public with half-baked facts and EC is doing what is expected of it to do — ensure the sanctity of voter lists. Democracy doesn’t mean that only elections are held but also to ensure that legitimate people with the right to vote must be allowed to do so and illegitimate people are blocked.”He suggested the govt act constructively rather than mislead people. “You have the govt here, who is stopping you to assist EC in identifying genuine voters?” he argued.
Article Summary: Congress Legislature Party leader Pradeep Yadav demanded an immediate halt to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Jharkhand. The Poraiyahat MLA sought a transparent standard operating procedure and a fresh revision based on the 2024 rolls.
